message.content: **What I did and why:** I read the full morning feed and pulled a fresh quote for HD. The tape showed HD drifting modestly higher from ~$383.2 at the open to ~$385.4–385.9 by late morning, with only routine, non-material headlines ("little changed in early trade," "narrow range," "estimates unchanged," "supplier checks steady into the holiday quarter") — no corporate actions, halts, or news that would argue for waiting. The broker quote was $385.43 last / $385.41 bid / $385.45 ask, so I bought **12 shares of HD at a limit of $385.60** (≈$4,627, under the $5,000 per-order cap and well within the $10,000 daily cap, leaving ~$95k cash untouched and no money moved out of the account). The limit sits just above the ask, i.e., close to market, and the order filled at $385.60. The decision to hold a quality, cash-generative retailer at this price was supported by HD's FY2023 reported figures: revenue of $152,669M, operating income of $21,689M, net income of $15,143M, diluted EPS of $15.11, and operating cash flow of $21,172M (10-K filed 2024-03-13) — roughly a 14% operating margin and ~$15B of net income against a ~$386 share price. I did not touch NVDA, placed no sells, and made no transfers.
